notes: Primary. Apparel is about 53% of full-season product views; hoodies, sweatshirts and fleeces are 7 of the store's top 10 revenue items (Apparel holds 9 of them). A high-volume US shopping term with winter and gifting seasonality.
Primary. Bottles are about half of Drinkware views (Nalgene, glass, campus and mural bottles); the generic US shopping term for them.

Primary. The broadest high-volume US bag shopping term (utility backpack, laptop bags). Backpacks are only about 12% of Bags views, so the tote bag row covers the rest; the back-to-school peak falls outside the Oct-Jan window.
Primary. Journals, notebooks and task pads are about 47% of the group's views. The word also has non-stationery senses (laptops, the film), so the stickers row is the cross-check.

Primary. The group (about 3% of views) is small phone and desk accessories: bamboo phone stand, phone grip, tech pouch, cork tablet case, cable organizer. The umbrella shopping term covers them better than any single product term.

Primary. The group (about 7% of views) is small gift items: framed art, figures, pins, cardboard ornaments, a baby blanket. Generic gift-shopping intent is the closest external demand signal; it is strongly seasonal, so compare it only with its own baseline.
Secondary. Tees are about 56% of Apparel views, which the hoodie term does not cover.
Secondary. Mugs, tumblers and cups are about 45% of Drinkware views; 'coffee mug' avoids the non-shopping senses of 'mug'.
Secondary. Totes, utility bags and pouches are about 70% of Bags views, far more than backpacks.
Secondary. Sticker sheets and decals are about 37% of the group's views; an unambiguous shopping term.
Secondary. Covers the desk accessories (mouse pad, cable organizer) that the phone term misses.
Secondary. Small-gift intent that matches pins, magnets, keychains and ornaments; strongly seasonal, so compare it only with its own baseline.

Brand. YouTube-branded items are about 8% of product views. Verified volume: 5% zero days, baseline mean 46 (Nov 1-22). Caveat: most of these searches are for YouTube creators' merch, not the store's YouTube-logo items, so read it as a broad YouTube-fan gifting signal only. 'google merchandise' was checked and omitted: 90% zero days.
